skill.name: executor-review
skill.description: Coordinate task reviews, scoped fix reviews, and final branch reviews using persistent verdict files and requirement-based findings.
skill.summary: Review implementation changes against contracts and preserve findings across bounded fix rounds.
skill.author: atri10

security_audit.summary: All 208 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, legitimate review commands, fixed sibling references, or protective secret-handling guidance. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, destructive intent, or audit-targeting prompt injection in the four reviewed files. Two semantic risks remain: security findings can be parked without mandatory human approval, and the main workflow hardcodes the final-review fork base.

remediation.issue: The round-cap workflow permits correctness findings to be parked without mandatory human approval for security issues.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit human approval before parking any security or data-loss finding, including non-credential issues. Keep affected tasks blocked until approval is recorded.

remediation.issue: The final-review example in SKILL.md hardcodes main, contradicting the final reviewer template.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve the fork base from recorded initiative provenance in every final-review command. Reject packages whose range does not match that provenance.

semantic_findings.title: Security Findings Lack Mandatory Human Approval at the Round Cap
semantic_findings.description: The breaker allows real findings to be parked when downstream work does not depend on them. Tasks can then be marked complete with parked findings. Only credential incidents have an explicit immediate human stop rule, leaving other security findings without mandatory human approval before deferral.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly permits parking real correctness findings and completing tasks. Final triage provides another check, but human approval is not required for every security deferral.

semantic_findings.title: Hardcoded Fork Base Can Produce an Incorrect Final Review Range
semantic_findings.description: The main workflow uses git merge-base main HEAD for final packaging. The final reviewer template requires the recorded fork base instead. For initiatives forked from another branch, this mismatch can review the wrong changes and undermine the final gate.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The two documented commands directly disagree about base selection. The final template explicitly explains why hardcoding main yields an incorrect range for other fork bases.

content.user_title: Review Tasks and Branches with Persistent Verdicts
content.value_statement: Implementation reviews lose traceability when findings exist only in conversation. This skill structures task, fix, and branch reviews around contract references and persistent verdict files.
actual_capabilities: Provides separate task-review assessments for specification compliance and code quality.
Defines persistent verdict files with review IDs, commit ranges, requirement citations, and finding counts.
Provides scoped re-review templates for finding closure, root-cause checks, and regression impact review.
Provides a final branch-review template for architecture conformance, cross-task dependencies, and deferred finding triage.
Defines bounded fix rounds, recorded rulings, and blocked responses for missing review inputs.
Requires secret findings to record locations and credential types without copying credential values.
limitations: Requires companion Executor scripts and contracts that are not included in these four files.
Requires valid plans, briefs, reports, review packages, and explicit template placeholder values.
Does not implement fixes or replace runtime verification and human merge decisions.
Round-cap security deferrals need human oversight, and the final-review example needs provenance-based fork selection.

use_cases.title: Review a Completed Implementation Task
use_cases.description: Compare a task diff with its brief and constraints, then preserve compliance and quality findings in a verdict file.

use_cases.title: Check Fixes Without Repeating the Full Review
use_cases.description: Assess each open finding against a fix diff and inspect affected callers for regressions before closing the round.

use_cases.title: Assess a Branch Before Verification
use_cases.description: Review cross-task dependencies, architecture contracts, and parked findings as one branch before handing recommended checks to verification.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Task Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review task [TASK_ID] using [BRIEF_FILE], [REPORT_FILE], and [DIFF_FILE]. Write compliance and quality verdicts to [VERDICT_FILE]. Report missing inputs as blocked.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: review a completed task with prepared inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Review Requirements and Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the task-review template for [TASK_ID]. Include [GLOBAL_CONSTRAINTS] verbatim with requirement IDs. Assess reported test evidence and list honest cannot-verify items.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: assess contract compliance and evidence coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Fix Round
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the re-review template with [PRIOR_VERDICT_FILE], [OPEN_FINDING_IDS], [REPORT_FILE], and [DIFF_FILE]. Review causal impact first. Write closure evidence to [VERDICT_FILE].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: verify finding closure and affected consumers.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Final Branch Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the final-review template for [PLAN_ID]. Resolve the fork base from provenance. Supply contracts and parked findings. Require human approval for security deferrals.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: assess branch coherence before separate runtime verification.

output_examples.input: Review a task whose error path lacks the behavior required by its brief.
output: Specification verdict: FAIL. The required error response is missing.
Code quality: NEEDS_FIXES. Finding I1 cites the changed error path and its requirement.
Gate: FAIL. The saved verdict identifies the review round and exact commit range.

output_examples.input: Re-review a fix that resolves one finding but breaks an affected caller.
output: Prior finding I1: ADDRESSED. The fix changes the documented root cause.
New important finding I1: An affected caller still uses the previous contract.
Gate: FAIL. The next round receives the new finding ID and supporting location.

output_examples.input: Perform a final branch review when the architecture phase was explicitly skipped.
output: Architecture conformance: NOT RUN. No architecture contract was authored.
Merge assessment: The missing architecture checks remain visible and need human consideration.
Recommended verification: Exercise the branch integration paths in the separate verification phase.

best_practices: Record exact base and head commits, use the recorded fork provenance, and validate each review package before dispatch.
Supply complete contract paths and preserve verdict files with unique review IDs and evidence-based findings.
Resolve cannot-verify items explicitly and require human approval before deferring security or data-loss findings.
anti_patterns: Substitute the last commit for the full task range or assume every initiative forked from main.
Pre-judge findings in dispatch prompts or treat implementer reports as independently verified evidence.
Overwrite another round's verdict or copy credential values into review artifacts.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It structures completed task reviews, scoped fix reviews, and final whole-branch reviews against supplied contracts.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. The workflow also requires file access, companion scripts, and reviewer dispatch support.

faq.question: Are the required scripts included?
faq.answer: No. The four reviewed files reference scripts from a companion Executor skill.

faq.question: Does review replace running tests?
faq.answer: No. Review checks reported evidence and permits focused checks for specific doubts. A separate verification phase owns broader runtime evidence.

faq.question: How are fixes tracked?
faq.answer: Each round uses a persistent verdict and finding IDs. Re-review marks prior findings addressed or not addressed and records new breakage.

faq.question: How should security findings be handled?
faq.answer: Record credential locations and types without copying values. Escalate credential incidents immediately, and require human approval before deferring other security findings.
